Predict the next state after each history

Source: R/predict.R
predict.transitiontrees.Rd

predict() predicts the state that follows each history from the longest context of a fitted tree that matches the end of that history. Histories longer than the tree's depth are read only as far back as the tree remembers, and histories whose recent states never formed a context fall back to a shorter suffix or to the root. The prediction is therefore always defined, and it uses as much of the past as the data supported when the tree was fitted.

It returns, for each history, the probability of every next state, or the most likely next state with type = "class". With tidy = TRUE it returns one row per history with the history, the context that was matched, the most likely next state and its probability, and the probability of every state.

To score observed sequences rather than predict from given histories, use score_positions(); to look up a single pathway, use query_pathway(); to fill in missing states, use impute_sequences().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'transitiontrees'
predict(object, newdata, type = c("prob", "class"), tidy = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

object

A transitiontrees object.

newdata

Histories, oldest state first: a list of character vectors, a wide data.frame or matrix with one history per row (missing or empty cells are dropped), or a single character vector. A history given as one arrow-notation string ("A -> B") is split into its states.

type

"prob" (default) for next-state probabilities or "class" for the most likely next state.

tidy

Return a data.frame with one row per history. Default FALSE.

...

Not used.

Value

With tidy = TRUE, a data.frame with one row per history and columns id (position in newdata), history (arrow notation; "(start)" when empty), context (the matched context), predicted (most likely next state), probability (its probability) and one column per state with the next-state probabilities. With tidy = FALSE and type = "prob", a numeric matrix with one row per history and one column per state, or a named vector when newdata is a single character vector; with type = "class", a character vector of most likely next states.

Conditions

transitiontrees_bad_input when newdata is not a list, data frame, matrix or character vector. A warning of class transitiontrees_unknown_state when a history contains a state outside the tree's alphabet; the prediction then uses the longest context after the last unknown state.

See also

query_pathway(), score_positions(), impute_sequences(), generate_sequences().

Examples

tree <- context_tree(trajectories, max_depth = 3)
histories <- list(c("Active", "Active"),
                  c("Average", "Disengaged", "Disengaged"),
                  character(0))
predict(tree, newdata = histories, tidy = TRUE)
#>   id                             history                             context
#> 1  1                    Active -> Active                    Active -> Active
#> 2  2 Average -> Disengaged -> Disengaged Average -> Disengaged -> Disengaged
#> 3  3                             (start)                             (start)
#>    predicted probability     Active   Average Disengaged
#> 1     Active   0.7852194 0.78521940 0.1939954 0.02078522
#> 2 Disengaged   0.6000000 0.02222222 0.3777778 0.60000000
#> 3    Average   0.4347594 0.37593583 0.4347594 0.18930481
predict(tree, newdata = histories, type = "class")
#> [1] "Active"     "Disengaged" "Average"
